name: HDFC Bank Ltd
about: HDFC Bank Limited (also known as HDFC) is an Indian banking and financial services company headquartered in Mumbai. It is India's largest private sector bank by assets and the world's tenth-largest bank by market capitalization as of May 2024. As of April 2024, HDFC Bank has a market capitalization of $145 billion, making it the third-largest company on the Indian stock exchanges. [1]

sections.one_liner: India's largest private bank after its merger; what matters now is whether margins recover from Q3 FY27 while profit growth lags loan growth.
business: Commercial bank licensed by the RBI, reported consolidated; HDFC Life is a subsidiary. Revenue mix by segment is not disclosed [AR FY26]
Retail is targeted at 60% of assets. Business banking grew 28% YoY, faster than wholesale, which management is deliberately slowing [Q1FY27 call, Q2FY27 call]
100M customers, adding 6-8M a year. 97% of payments and service transactions are digital; 5 AI use cases are live [Q4FY26 call]
Related-party derivatives limit with HDFC Life raised from ₹900 Cr to ₹2,500 Cr notional. ₹60,000 Cr of Tier I/II bonds authorised [AR FY26]
financial_snapshot: Q2 FY27: revenue ₹95,132 Cr, +9.4% YoY and +5.0% QoQ. PAT ₹21,537 Cr, +5.8% YoY, so profit grew slower than revenue [Numbers]
TTM: revenue ₹3,59,956 Cr, PAT ₹83,685 Cr, +11.5% YoY. EBITDA/OPM are negative and not meaningful for a bank [Numbers]
ROE 13.6%, ROCE 7.0%. Management cites ROA of 1.8%, GNPA of 1.11% and credit cost of 44bps [Numbers, Q2FY27 call]
P/E 13.3, P/B 1.76x (₹690 vs ₹391 book), dividend yield 1.9%. Stock is 32% below its ₹1,018 high and 3% above its ₹669 low [Numbers]
trajectory: 3-year revenue CAGR of 26.9% is inflated by the merger: FY24 revenue jumped 66%. Underlying growth was FY25 +18.6%, then FY26 only +3.6% [Numbers]
PAT growth is slowing: FY24 +41.8%, FY25 +12.2%, FY26 +7.9%. 5-year PAT CAGR is 20.0% [Numbers]
Quarterly revenue was flat near ₹87,000 Cr for 5 quarters (YoY growth fell to 0.5%), then jumped to ₹95,132 Cr in Sep-26 [Numbers]
Loans grew 15.3% while revenue grew 9.4%. That 6-point gap implies yields compressed, consistent with management calling the margin bottom in Q2 [Numbers, Q2FY27 call]
balance_sheet: Borrowings are 11% of funding vs the industry's 5-6%, a costly merger legacy. CASA is 34% vs 38% before the merger [Q1FY27 call]
Deposits +18.8% vs loans +15.3% YoY, so funding is catching up. LCR of 113% is below the 115% ideal [Q2FY27 call]
Capital adequacy 19.7%; risk weights 69% of assets. ₹60,000 Cr bond authorisation adds capital headroom. Debt/equity is not disclosed [Q4FY26 call, Q2FY27 call, AR FY26]
cash_quality: CFO/PAT swings widely: 0.45x FY23, 0.29x FY24, 1.73x FY25, 1.43x FY26. For a bank this reflects deposit/loan flows, not earnings quality [Numbers]
Capex is steady at ₹3,400-4,200 Cr a year (CFO minus FCF), about 4% of FY26 PAT. Growth uses little fixed capital [Numbers]
Profit converts to cash mainly through capital: the 1.9% yield implies about ₹20,000 Cr of dividends, roughly 24% of TTM PAT [Numbers]
narrative_vs_numbers: Management says Q2 PAT was +12.7% ex-trading gains; consolidated PAT was +5.8%. The 'Rs 19.5bn' figure doesn't match ₹21,537 Cr consolidated [Q2FY27 call, Numbers]
Q1 call said reported profit growth was 5%; consolidated Jun-26 PAT shows +19.3% YoY. The standalone vs consolidated bases are unreconciled [Q1FY27 call, Numbers]
FY26 'net income +11%' vs consolidated PAT +7.9% and revenue +3.6%. Profit beat revenue growth through costs and provisions, not the core spread [Q4FY26 call, Numbers]
Story and numbers agree on growth: loans 15.3% vs 12% in FY26, and Q2 revenue +5.0% QoQ after five flat quarters [Q2FY27 call, Numbers]
guidance: Margin bottomed in Q2 FY27; 'trajectory will be upward from the next quarter', helped by the October 25bps repo hike [Q2FY27 call]
Business banking to grow 18-21% a year; LCR to stay at 110-120% [Q4FY26 call]
Profit growth should match or beat balance-sheet growth over the long term. Cost of funds can fall 40-50bps, but slowly [Q1FY27 call]
Long-term targets: borrowings down from 11% to 5-6%, CASA back to about 38%, retail at 60% of assets [Q1FY27 call]
Headcount flat for 3-4 years. The new MD will set out growth, margin and productivity plans 'next month' [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.delivered: Dec-26 quarter not yet reported; Sep-26 PAT +5.8% vs revenue +9.4%

LCR 113%, inside the band but below the 115% ideal [Q2FY27 call]

ledger.delivered: Deposits +18.8% YoY, but FCNR mix raised funding costs; margin hit bottom

ledger.promised: Keep growth momentum; FY26 credit growth was 12% [Q4FY26 call]
ledger.delivered: AUM +15.3%; Sep-26 revenue +9.4% YoY after 0.5% in Mar-26

ledger.promised: Profit growth at or above balance-sheet growth [Q1FY27 call]
Customer acquisition improves within nine months [Q1FY27 call]
ledger.delivered: Liability relationships 1.7M, +25% QoQ; new cards 1.4M, +19% QoQ; window still open

bull: 13.3x P/E and 1.76x book for 13.6% ROE and 1.11% GNPA. Stock is 3% above its 52-week low [Numbers, Q2FY27 call]
Revenue +5.0% QoQ after five flat quarters; repo hike plus margin bottom could lift profit growth back above 15% [Numbers, Q2FY27 call]
Cutting borrowings from 11% to 6% and the 40-50bps cost-of-funds gain both mechanically lift margins over time [Q1FY27 call]
bear: PAT growth has lagged loan growth for 3 years (FY26 +7.9%). Q2 PAT +5.8% shows growth isn't yet turning into profit [Numbers]
Governance overhang: March 2026 chairman exit cited ethics and the board 'didn't give any specific explanation'. New MD strategy is still unannounced [Mar 2026 call, Q2FY27 call]
Margin drags: retail back-book runs off 20-30% a year, FCNR funding costs, draft cuts to insurance commissions, monsoon risk to agri/MSME loans [Q2FY27 call]
questions: Reconcile the '+12.7% ex-trading' PAT claim with consolidated PAT growth of 5.8%.
How many basis points of margin expansion in Q3 FY27 from the repo hike?
With LCR at 113%, how much loan growth is possible before needing 115%?
Will the new MD keep the 60% retail, 38% CASA and 5-6% borrowing targets?

transcripts.label: Oct 2026
transcripts.tone_evidence: Confident on momentum, asset quality, tech; defensive on margin pressure, deposit mix, outflows masking growth.

guidance.statement: Margin trajectory at bottom in Q2, neutral to positive outlook ahead
guidance.quote: The trajectory will be upward from the next quarter onwards.

guidance.statement: 25bps repo increase in October should be factored into P&L by December
guidance.quote: 25 basis points change...in October should largely be factored in by December.

guidance.statement: Target operating band 110-120%, ideally 115%, needed for sustainable growth
guidance.quote: we would like to operate between 110 and 120

guidance.statement: Employee count to remain flat, then increase in 3-4 years as productivity matures
guidance.quote: remain flat and probably...start to increase over maybe three, four years' time

guidance.statement: Retail ex-agri loan growth improving; 20-30% annual runoff requires continued acceleration
guidance.quote: across the next 2 quarters, you will see that change coming through

guidance.statement: New MD to present perspective on growth, margins, quality and productivity soon
guidance.quote: I will soon present a perspective on growth, margins, quality and productivity

themes: Operational rigor and daily productivity gains in retail/MSME sales and service delivery
AI and digital technology embedded across customer experience, fraud prevention, collections
Balance sheet rebalancing toward retail/MSME growth, moderating corporate exposure
Liability franchise expansion via branch productivity and deposit relationship acquisition
Industry-leading asset quality maintained despite credit growth acceleration
Rate cycle inflection: margin bottom reached, tailwinds from 25bps repo increase
analyst_pushback: Why margin decline similar to peers despite lower corporate growth? Kaizad: retail backbook runoff 20-30% annually; improvement expected next 2 quarters.
When will retail deposit proportion increase? Sashi: extraordinary outflows masking momentum; structural adjustments and alternate non-deposit strategies coming soon.
LCR at 113% below 110-115% target—constraint on growth? Srini: used for growth dynamics; need to maintain ~115% for sustained loan growth.
Why not reduce lower-yield corporate assets like other banks? Kaizad: relationship management more important; certain retail products match wholesale returns.

segments.comment: Primary business; specifics not detailed in opening pages
